item.title: City to celebrate birthday
item.description: Newton will celebrate its 154th birthday with a community party and other special events this month.

item.title: Wichita organist’s recital spans several eras
item.description: YunJung “YJ” Lee sees her organ playing as an offering to God and an invitation to listeners to draw closer to the divine.

item.title: Hesston College honored MLK Day through community service projects
item.description: HESSTON, Kan. — In recognition of Martin Luther King Jr. Day last week, Hesston College students, faculty and staff dedicated themselves to serving the local community by participating in more than a dozen service projects throughout Hesston and Newton.

item.title: Kennedy Center: Don’t Mend It, End It
item.description: After only two weeks on the job, The Hill reports, Kevin Couch resigned in late January as head of artistic programming at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.

item.title: Bethel names long-time Excel finance administrator to VP position
item.description: Karen Hiebert, rural Hesston, began Jan. 12 as vice president for business and finance at Bethel College.

item.title: Despite cold, Kansas Day clebrated
item.description: Kauffman Museum’s annual Kansas Day celebration, which this year focused on food, was able to operate despite bitter cold temperatures on Jan. 30 — it was about 19 degrees at noon when the event started.
